as_told.title: The Telepathy Tapes: nonverbal children communicating on the hill

plain: The Telepathy Tapes, a 2024 podcast, reports on dozens of autistic people who cannot speak and who seem to share a telepathic link with a caregiver, usually their mother. The researcher Matthew Pines retells it, crediting the work of Diane Hennacy Powell, a researcher who studies these patients. He calls it the "remarkable story" of people who report "a telepathic connection" with one caregiver. The scientist Don Hoffman does not name the podcast but says he has looked at studies where an autistic child "is able to read what's in their mother's mind." He says some of the designs seemed "pretty rigorous." Retired Navy admiral Tim Gallaudet mentions Powell's work with autistic patients as her own long-running research. The former Senate staffer Kirk McConnell adds that these people seem to connect with each other "across vast distances." Michels, in his own telling, describes the children communicating and gathering on what they call "the hill". If true, minds would be able to reach each other without words or senses.
